 entertainment Chew Chor Meng leaves Mediacorp after 36 years
 Chew Chor Meng left Mediacorp after 36 years. PHOTO: Instagram/The Celebrity Agency PUBLISHED ON November 03, 2026 6:45 AM BY Yeo Shu Hui Chew Chor Meng announces his departure from Mediacorp after 36 years.
 The Celebrity Agency, who managed the 57-year-old local actor, shared in an Instagram post today (Nov 3): " Over the past 36 years, he has endeared himself to audiences through a wide range of memorable roles, from the lovable Ah Bee in the long-running sitcom Don't Worry, Be Happy to his Best Actor-winning performance in Hainan Kopi Tales.
 "His versatility and enduring appeal have made him one of Singapore's most beloved television personalities, with his contributions to local entertainment recognised through the Special Achievement Award at Star Awards 2019.
 "We sincerely thank Chor Meng for his dedication and the many contributions he has made over the years and wish him good health and all the very best in his next chapter."
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by The Celebrity Agency (@the_celebrityagency) 
 Chor Meng also reflected on his close to four decades in showbiz in an Instagram post today.
 He wrote: "36 years of acting career, in a blink of an eye, has become one of the most precious memories of my life.
 "No regrets, only full of gratitude. Because for the past 36 years, I have loved, worked hard, and was blissful.
 "I want to thank everyone who had given me the opportunities and encouragement along the way, and the audience for their love and support over the years.
 "My life on stage is over, but the wonderful life goes on."
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by Rafael 周初明 (@chewchormeng) 
 Chor Meng debuted in local showbiz in 1990 after winning Star Search that same year. Besides acting, he also ventured into hosting local variety shows, including City Beat (1995), True Files (2005, 2006 and 2007) and Kungfu Chef (2005, 2006).
 In 2008, he suffered from Kennedy's disease — a rare inherited neuromuscular disorder that causes progressive weakening and wasting of muscles, particularly in the arms and legs.
 He shared during an episode of Hear U Out in 2020 that at the time of his diagnosis, he was given 18 months to live and had considered ending his life because of his various struggles.
 In 2023, Chor Meng said in an interview that he intended to continue acting despite his illness and expressed his gratification towards everyone who enabled him.
 Since 2017, Chor Meng, who is married with two daughters, also ventured into food and beverage businesses, partnering local DJ-actor Dennis Chew and friends in businesses including 888 Mookata, Viewdee Thai Bistro, The Famous Zhou, as well as Tam Chiak Kopitiam .
